output.name: Varo — The Unpaid Crossing (The Unflown)
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the first things to drift past the last lamp were the drowned, and none knew the way. A boatman, grey-bearded and thin as a gutting knife, took a shell coin from a drowned woman's hand and laid it on his palm. That was the fare. He rowed her out past the edge of the wind, by the Turned Wake where Aun's boat tipped, and into the dark the Unflown keeps. He has not given the coin back. In the north-east Tirun, the Upturned Hull, floats keel-up with her lamps still lit under the thwarts, and the old ones say a boatman's lamp burns longer than his oil. Mother Hesk counts every string in Vel and has counted this one missing. Kael casts for the boat each night and brings up only weed. Tavo blows past the stern and laughs, because he cannot be bargained with. Sil looks down from her lamp, searching among the drowned for Aun. So the old ones say, mending nets: pay the fare when you are ready to be ferried, and never ask the boatman for change.
output.finding: Sailors far to the south find Varo by starting at Ulsena, the Kelp Bride, and sighting three-quarters of a hand-span (about 15°) to her west, where the boatman's lamp sits low over the edge of the wind.
